root_cause: This is a recurrence of the exact same failure signature first recorded on 2026-09-21 (run 35611485728) for this same PR (#38190). The job_llm_accuracy_tests.yml workflow installs the locally-built 'openvino' and 'openvino_tokenizers' wheels via install_ov_wheels, but the subsequent 'pip install -r tests/llm/requirements.txt' step pulls in 'whowhatbench', which transitively depends on 'optimum-intel[nncf,tests]' -> 'openvino-genai'. Pip resolves and installs prebuilt 'openvino-genai-2026.4.0.0' and 'openvino-tokenizers-2026.4.0.0' wheels from the proxy index, silently uninstalling the just-installed local 'openvino-tokenizers-2026.4.1.0' wheel in the process. The 'openvino_genai' native extension expects a matching libopenvino.so.2640 that was never actually provisioned in this environment (only the locally-built core 'openvino' 2026.4.1 wheel is present, without the SOVERSION the genai wheel was linked against), so the import fails at collection time before any test runs.
reproduction_steps: In a fresh venv: 1) pip install <local openvino-2026.4.1 wheel> <local openvino_tokenizers-2026.4.1.0 wheel>; 2) pip install -r tests/llm/requirements.txt (pulls whowhatbench -> optimum-intel[nncf,tests] -> openvino-genai from the index); 3) python3 -c "import openvino_genai" reproduces 'ImportError: libopenvino.so.2640: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory'.
recommended_actions: Pin/constrain 'openvino-genai' and 'openvino-tokenizers' in tests/llm/requirements.txt (or tests/llm/constraints.txt) so pip cannot silently swap the locally-built wheels for mismatched prebuilt ones during transitive resolution of whowhatbench/optimum-intel.

Install openvino-genai explicitly from the same locally-built artifact set as 'openvino'/'openvino_tokenizers' via install_ov_wheels, before running 'pip install -r tests/llm/requirements.txt', and pass '--no-deps' (or an equivalent constraint) on the requirements install to prevent it from re-resolving/overwriting those packages.

Add a fast-fail 'python3 -c "import openvino_genai"' smoke-check step immediately after wheel installation in job_llm_accuracy_tests.yml, so this ABI/version mismatch surfaces clearly instead of as a pytest collection error.

Since this is the second occurrence for the same PR, consider flagging to the PR author/CI infra owner that the fix from the first occurrence (2026-09-21, run 35611485728) has not yet been applied to job_llm_accuracy_tests.yml or tests/llm/requirements.txt.
prevention_strategies: Add explicit version constraints (or install-from-local-wheel steps) for openvino-genai and openvino-tokenizers in tests/llm/requirements.txt / constraints.txt so pip cannot silently substitute a mismatched prebuilt runtime during transitive dependency resolution. Add a CI smoke-import step right after wheel installation for any job that installs additional OpenVINO-dependent python packages, so ABI mismatches fail fast with a clear message instead of as an opaque pytest collection error.
historical_context: Identical failure signature (a87e95431b0e8175) was first recorded on 2026-09-21T15:45:59Z in run 35611485728, also for PR #38190, affecting both the CPU and iGPU LLM accuracy jobs. This is the second occurrence of the same unresolved issue; the recommended constraint/pin fix from the first investigation does not appear to have been applied yet.
